text:
Dmitry Orlov is 35 and playing some of the best offensive hockey of his career. He has 11 points in his last ten games, including three assists against Seattle on Saturday, and 17 on the season with ten on the power play. He is one assist from 300. San Jose Hockey Now wrote that he and Mason Marchment are finding their games, and the numbers agree: he is getting a little more of his own chances too, even with his ice time down two minutes a night.

The caution is five on five. The Sharks take 41% of the expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), worse than without him, so most of this is power-play value, which is also what Evolving-Hockey saw last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking does credit him at his own line, where he stops 15% of the entries aimed at him against 11% for a typical defenseman. A Stanley Cup winner with Washington in 2018, he quarterbacks PP1 for a young team. Our range has him around 40 points.
